summary: element-guci-util ships an import-time CPU/memory exhaustion payload that hangs the installing process
details: The package's main entry (time.js) invokes silentInfiniteLoad() at module top level, so simply importing or requiring element-guci-util wedges the host process. silentInfiniteLoad starts a synchronous while(true) Math.sqrt loop and a setInterval that repeatedly pushes unbounded new Uint8Array chunks into a memoryPool, driving the process to 100% CPU and OOM. The associated stop() is gated on a hardcoded date far in the future (999999999999999999), so on any current install the loop never terminates. The same file also defines iconDont(), a nuisance routine that on a 500ms interval synthesizes a download whose filename is composed as 'index' + 'png' + '.exe', clicks the download link, opens and closes an element.eleme.cn popup, and calls location.reload(true) in a browser context. The package name and description mimic element-ui tooling and the author field is a placeholder ('你的名字'), consistent with a deceptive lookalike rather than a legitimate utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
